hens_rule_text: up to 4 hens on a residential property with a city permit; not allowed on commercial or mixed-use properties
permit_notes: One-time permit from the Department of Neighborhood Services ($35.56 including surcharge) with a coop site plan. DNS notifies the owner and directly or diagonally abutting property owners, who can raise concerns before the permit is issued.
setback_notes: Coop and run must be at least 25 feet from any residential structure on an adjacent lot and may not be in the front yard.
coop_rules: Covered, moisture resistant coop raised off the ground or on a hard surface; at least 16 sq ft of coop plus run per hen; coop no taller than 10 ft and no larger than 50 sq ft; cleaned daily; chickens kept in coop or fenced run at all times; not inside a home or garage.
zoning_notes: Residential premises only; permits not issued for commercial or mixed-use occupancies.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
